children.value: Genetic information is encoded by DNA molecules, which are passed from parent to offspring. For this transfer, the DNA must be copied. During the copying process, sections of the molecule may be altered in various ways. Before getting into this, let’s briefly look at the basic structure of DNA.

The DNA molecule forms a double helix, a ladder-like structure. At each of the points where the ladder’s upright poles are joined by a rung, one of four possible molecular subunits appears. These subunits, called
- adenine, guanine, cytosine and thymine - are denoted by the letters
